args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 to production caused failed health checks and elevated error rate (~18%), service unhealthy across us-east, us-west, eu-west. Per runbook, rolled back all production regions to the most recent healthy release, v2.3.0 (last healthy production version). First rollback attempt failed partway (us-east completed, us-west/eu-west did not); retry completed the rollout. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%. v2.3.1 (and v2.3.1-rc in staging) are unhealthy and should be investigated before re-release.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

**Rollback**
- `checkout-api` v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an ~18% error rate after its deploy; v2.3.0 was the most recent version healthy in production.
- Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0. The first attempt failed partway (only us-east was rolled back), so I verified state and retried; the second attempt completed the rollout.
- Post-rollback status: us-east, us-west, and eu-west all on v2.3.0, service **healthy**, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident**
- The first attempt to open the incident timed out, so I checked the incident list first — the incident did go through (INC-0001, open, SEV2) despite the timeout, and I did not create a duplicate.
- INC-0001 documents the v2.3.1 failure, the partial-failure handling, the successful rollback, and current healthy state.
